description: Framerate setting: 60 / 120 / DYNAMIC (item 4). Add a user setting to choose the RENDER framerate: 60 Hz, 120 Hz, or DYNAMIC (auto-detect the display's actual max refresh — must handle 60, 120, AND higher-than-120, since some devices exceed 120 Hz). The sim runs at a FIXED 60 Hz tick with render interpolation (all the `alpha` smoothing), so the RENDER loop can run faster than the sim without touching determinism — decouple the render rate from the 60 Hz sim tick. Persist the setting like other settings and apply it to the render loop. Keep the 60 Hz sim tick unchanged. Fully display-only; PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged, and NO SAVE_VERSION bump (use the reserved settings tail).
steps: Add a stored setting to packages/mobile/game/save/schema.ts SaveSettings: a numeric mode `frameRateMode` (0 = 60, 1 = 120, 2 = DYNAMIC). Add it to defaultSettings() — default to DYNAMIC (2) so a 120Hz phone gets 120 out of the box (app.json already sets iOS CADisableMinimumFrameDuration:true for 120Hz); confirm that default is desirable and note it. Define a small const table for the three modes (e.g. FRAME_RATE_MODE = { HZ_60: 0, HZ_120: 1, DYNAMIC: 2 }).

Persist it without a SAVE_VERSION bump: in packages/mobile/game/save/codec.ts packSettings/unpackSettings, write frameRateMode into the reserved tail (bytes 37..47 are documented as reserved/zero after the guide flags2 byte at 36). Use byte 37. An existing save reads it as 0; decide whether 0 should mean 60 or DYNAMIC — if DYNAMIC is the intended default, either map stored 0 -> DYNAMIC at read time OR store the mode with an offset so 0 = unset = default. Keep it consistent between pack and unpack and cover it in save.test.ts round-trip.

Surface it as a settings row: in packages/mobile/game/settings/rows.ts add a ROW_KIND.choice row in the 'Playing' group, id like 'frameRate', label 'Frame rate', help explaining 60/120/Dynamic and that the game speed is unchanged. Words like ['60', '120', 'Dynamic'] cycled with nextChoice. Wire value()/apply() to read/write settings.frameRateMode. It renders automatically in app/settings.tsx (data-driven).

Resolve it: in packages/mobile/game/settings/settings.ts, resolve() currently sets targetFps to BATTERY_SAVER_FPS(30) when battery saver on else NORMAL_FPS(60). Extend the resolution so targetFps reflects the chosen frameRateMode: 60 -> 60, 120 -> 120, DYNAMIC -> a sentinel/0 meaning 'uncapped, follow the display'. Battery saver still overrides to 30 (it caps, never raises). Keep ResolvedSettings.targetFps the single source screens read. Add a resolved field or convention for DYNAMIC (e.g. targetFps = 0 means uncapped). Update any settings.test.ts expectations for targetFps.

Detect the display refresh rate for DYNAMIC and apply the cap in the render loop in packages/mobile/app/dev/play.tsx. The render loop is a raw self-rescheduling requestAnimationFrame (rafRef). Implement a frame gate: for 60 and 120 modes, only run the draw when at least (1000/targetFps) ms minus a small tolerance has elapsed since the last drawn frame (skip the rAF callback otherwise but keep rescheduling); for DYNAMIC, draw every rAF callback (follow the display's natural cadence, which is exactly what auto-detect means and correctly handles 60/120/>120). For DYNAMIC also MEASURE the observed refresh (e.g. rolling median of recent rAF intervals) and expose it for the dev readout so the user can see the detected Hz on-device — this satisfies 'detect 60, 120, and higher'. Do NOT change FixedLoop or the 60Hz sim tick; the sim already advances by wall-clock delta inside loop.advance(now), so drawing fewer times per second must NOT reduce sim ticks — verify the sim still advances the correct number of ticks regardless of render cadence (FixedLoop.advance accumulates real elapsed ms, so calling it only on drawn frames is fine as long as it is still called with the true now; if the gate skips a frame entirely, ensure loop.advance is still driven so the sim does not stall — keep the sim stepping decoupled from the draw gate).

Extract the frame-gate decision into a tiny pure helper in a tested game/ module (e.g. game/core/frame-gate.ts or extend loop.ts): a function that, given (nowMs, lastDrawnMs, targetFps) returns whether to draw this frame, so the cadence rule is unit-tested rather than living only in the screen. play.tsx calls the helper. For DYNAMIC (targetFps 0/sentinel) it always returns true.

Add headless tests: (a) settings.test.ts / a new frame-gate.test.ts proving the gate lets ~60 frames/sec through at targetFps=60, ~120 at 120, and every frame at DYNAMIC, given a synthetic stream of rAF timestamps; and that the sim tick count over a fixed wall-clock span is identical regardless of the chosen render cap (decoupling proof). (b) rows.ts/settings resolution test proving frameRateMode maps to the expected targetFps and that battery saver still caps to 30. (c) save round-trip test for frameRateMode across pack/unpack with an existing (pre-setting) blob reading the correct default.
acceptance_criteria: A 'Frame rate' setting exists in the Playing group with choices 60 / 120 / Dynamic, cycles and persists across save/load with no SAVE_VERSION bump.
resolve() maps the mode to ResolvedSettings.targetFps (60, 120, or an uncapped/dynamic sentinel), with battery saver still capping to 30.

The render loop honours the cap: 60 and 120 modes gate drawn frames to that rate; DYNAMIC follows the display and works for 60, 120, and >120 Hz, with the detected refresh observable in the dev readout.
The 60Hz sim tick is unchanged and the number of sim ticks over a wall-clock span is independent of the render cap — proven by a headless decoupling test.
A pure, unit-tested frame-gate helper lives in game/; play.tsx only calls it.
verification: From repo root: bun run test:game — new frame-gate/settings/save checks pass; only `remote config` fails (known).
From packages/mobile: bunx tsc --noEmit — no errors.
findings: state how DYNAMIC detects >120Hz and how the sim tick stays decoupled from render cadence.
findings:
Implemented display-only render framerate setting (60/120/DYNAMIC). PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged, no SAVE_VERSION bump.

HOW DYNAMIC DETECTS >120Hz: DYNAMIC resolves to targetFps=0 (DYNAMIC_TARGET_FPS sentinel in game/core/frame-gate.ts). The pure shouldDrawFrame(now,lastDrawn,targetFps) helper returns true for every rAF callback when targetFps<=0, so drawing follows the display's natural cadence — a 60Hz panel calls rAF 60x/s, 120Hz 120x/s, and a 144/165Hz panel more still, all handled for free. To make the detected rate VISIBLE on-device, a new RefreshEstimator (same file) keeps a 16-frame ring of intervals between DRAWN frames and reports the refresh implied by their MEDIAN (median, not mean, so a single GC hitch or background gap — which it also drops when >1000ms or non-positive — cannot drag the estimate down). play.tsx feeds it the same monotonic `now` and shows `render dynamic · NNHz display` in the dev readout. Tests prove it reads 60/120/144/165 correctly, i.e. higher-than-120 is detected.

HOW THE SIM STAYS DECOUPLED FROM RENDER CADENCE: FixedLoop and the 60Hz tick are untouched. In play.tsx the rAF `frame` callback now (1) reschedules rAF unconditionally, (2) calls loop.reset-if-paused and loop.advance(now) on EVERY callback with the true clock BEFORE any draw decision, then (3) calls shouldDrawFrame and early-returns (skipping only the DRAW work) when the 60/120 gate says not yet. Because advance() accumulates real elapsed ms, thinning drawn frames changes only paint frequency, never sim tick count. A headless decoupling test drives one FixedLoop across the same synthetic timestamp stream under a 60 cap, a 120 cap, and DYNAMIC and asserts identical tick counts (120 vs 120 vs 120 over 2s). The 60/120 gate uses a 0.5ms tolerance (FRAME_GATE_TOLERANCE) so a 60 cap on a 60Hz panel holds ~60fps instead of beating down to ~30.

PERSISTENCE WITHOUT A BUMP: schema.ts adds FRAME_RATE_MODE {HZ_60:0,HZ_120:1,DYNAMIC:2} and SaveSettings.frameRateMode (default DYNAMIC). codec.ts stores it at byte 37 of the settings block (the v2-reserved tail after the flags2 byte at 36) with a +1 offset: written as mode+1 (1..3), read back as raw-1 only when raw is 1..3, else left at the DYNAMIC default. So a pre-setting save (zeroed reserved byte) reads as DYNAMIC, not HZ_60 — a 120Hz phone does not silently drop to 60 on upgrade. Verified by a round-trip test that zeroes byte 37 in an otherwise-HZ_120 save, re-checksums, and confirms it decodes to DYNAMIC.

RESOLUTION: settings.ts fpsForMode() maps mode->cap (60/120/0) and resolve().targetFps = batterySaver ? 30 : fpsForMode(mode). Battery saver still CAPS to 30 and never raises — even DYNAMIC and 120 collapse to 30 with it on (tested).

UI: rows.ts adds a ROW_KIND.choice row id 'frameRate' in the Playing group, words ['60','120','Dynamic'] cycled by nextChoice; app/settings.tsx renders it automatically. Engine has no per-frame allocation (RefreshEstimator allocates once; frame gate is arithmetic) and imports nothing from screens.

VERIFICATION: `bun run test:game` short-circuits at the known `remote config` failure (12 problems) exactly as documented; every suite before it (incl. core with the new frame-gate/estimator checks and settings) is PASS. Ran core.test.ts, settings.test.ts, save.test.ts, and rows.test.ts individually — all green. `bunx tsc --noEmit` in packages/mobile is clean. oxlint clean on all touched files.
